description: REVIEWER-FIX ABLATION: lgbm_direct with CAUSAL covariates, weather domain -- the critical test of whether the 'domain flip' (lgbm wins weather) is real forecasting skill or a perfect-foresight artifact (weather covariates near-deterministic of temperature target)
command: python run_forecast.py cities --source weather_csv --data-dir data/weather --pm25-window-dir data/cities_final --manifest cities_manifest.csv --retrain-per-fold --folds 6 --causal-covariates --out-prefix results/v1/weather_panel/causal_ablation
notes: CPU-only, parallel; compared post-hoc vs canonical chronos (R005/R013). HEADLINE-CRITICAL. VERDICT (L-027, analysis/causal_covariate_ablation.py): the 'specialist wins weather' headline is a PERFECT-FORESIGHT ARTIFACT. lgbm with perfect future weather beats chronos 26/29 cities (p=1.4e-6, mean 0.533 vs 0.792); lgbm with realistic causal covariates (last-known weather) only 16/29, p=0.29 -> statistical TIE with chronos (0.745 vs 0.792). Foresight worth +0.212 MASE in weather (p=2.6e-8) vs ~0 in PM2.5. CONCLUSION: under realistic covariate availability, the zero-shot FM is competitive with the tuned specialist in BOTH domains; the specialist's apparent weather edge requires an unrealistic perfect NWP forecast. This reframes the paper's central claim -- abstract must NOT say 'specialists win weather forecasting' unconditionally.
